name: Bitterness and an Unforgiving Heart

counsel.text: Mortification of sin is peculiarly from the death of Christ. It is one peculiar, yea, eminent end of the death of Christ, which shall assuredly be accomplished by it. He died to destroy the works of the devil. Whatever came upon our natures by his first temptation, whatever receives strength in our persons by his daily suggestions, Christ died to destroy it all.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

counsel.text: Be acquainted, then, with thine own heart: though it be deep, search it; though it be dark, inquire into it; though it give all its distempers other names than what are their due, believe it not.
counsel.author: John Owen

counsel.text: We remember injuries: this is to fill a precious cabinet with dung; but as Hierom saith, how soon do we forget the sacred truths of God?
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 2

counsel.text: Let us be like Christ in mildness and sweetness. Let us pray for our enemies, and conquer them by love. David's kindness melted Saul's heart.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: A Body of Divinity, Christ's humiliation in his incarnation

counsel.text: What! Because he has wronged you, will you therefore wrong God? Is it not doing wrong to God to take his work out of his hand?
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the sixth commandment

counsel.text: The Israelites did eat the Passover with bitter herbs; so must we eat the sacrament with bitter herbs of repentance, but not with bitter hearts of wrath and malice. The hearts of the communicants should be knit together with the bond of love.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the Lord's Supper

counsel.text: It is sad to consider that saints should have many eyes to behold one another's infirmities, and not one eye to see each other's graces, that they should use spectacles to behold one another's weaknesses, rather than looking-glasses to behold one another's graces.
counsel.author: Thomas Brooks

counsel.text: Ah! souls, it is not a base, low thing, but a God-like thing, though we are wronged by others, yet to be the first in seeking after peace.
counsel.author: Thomas Brooks

counsel.text: Flesh and blood would bid a man call for fire from heaven, rather than mercy to fall upon them that so cruelly handle them. He that can forgive his enemy is too hard for him, and hath the better of him: because his enemy's blows do but bruise his flesh, but the wounds that love gives pierce the soul and conscience.
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: Possibly thou hast a grudge against thy neighbour. The fire is kindled in thy heart, though it flames not presently out into bitter words and angry behaviour; and thou art going to pray. Ask now thy soul, whether God will accept that sacrifice which is kindled with such strange fire? Yea, bid thy soul bethink herself how thy hopes of pardoning and saving mercy from God can agree with thy wrathful unforgiving spirit towards thy brother?
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: The church of Christ is a common hospital, wherein all are in some measure sick of some spiritual disease or other; that we should all have ground of exercising mutually the spirit of wisdom and meekness.
counsel.author: Richard Sibbes

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.text: Gracious Father, you have forgiven me a debt I could never pay, and you have cast all my sins behind your back. I come to you through Jesus Christ. I confess that I have held on to bitterness. I have kept a record of wrongs, replayed old injuries in my mind, and quietly wished harm on those who hurt me. I have lived every day on your forgiveness while refusing to give mine. I have told myself that my resentment was justice, when it was really a way of keeping the wrong alive and keeping myself on the throne. A root of bitterness has grown in me, and it has troubled me and defiled others. This is sin against you, who command me to forgive as you in Christ have forgiven me. Lord, have mercy on me. Christ prayed for those who nailed him to the cross, and his blood speaks a better word than the blood of Abel. For his sake forgive me, and give me a heart that forgives from within. Holy Spirit, pull up this root and heal what has festered. Where justice must still be sought, let me seek it without malice. I thank you that vengeance belongs to you, that you judge rightly, and that I am free to let go. In Jesus' name. Amen.

prayers.title: When old hurts return
prayers.text: Lord, the old wound is open again, and I feel the bitterness rising. I bring it to you instead of feeding it. You saw what was done to me, and you will judge justly; I do not have to carry this. Keep me from replaying it again. Lord Jesus, you were betrayed, mocked, and forsaken, and you forgave. Let your forgiveness of me loom larger in my mind than their sin against me. Give me grace to bless and not to curse, and to pray for the one who wronged me, even now. Holy Spirit, soften what has grown hard. Amen.

prayers.title: For a forgiving heart
prayers.text: Father, make me tenderhearted. Put away from me all bitterness, wrath, anger, clamor, and slander, with all malice. Teach me to forgive as you have forgiven me in Christ: freely, fully, and without keeping score. Show me where I have taken pleasure in resentment, and let that pleasure die. Where peace can be made, give me courage to seek it; where it cannot, give me rest in leaving the matter with you. Remind me how often others have had to bear with me. Fill my heart with the love that covers a multitude of sins, and make me a peacemaker in my home and my church. Through Jesus Christ. Amen.

prayers.title: Confessing unpeaceableness toward others
prayers.text: We have been verily guilty concerning our brother; for we have not studied the things that make for peace, nor things wherewith we might edify one another. We have been ready to judge our brother, and to set at nought our brother, forgetting that we must all shortly stand before the judgment-seat of Christ.
prayers.author: Matthew Henry

prayers.title: That all bitterness may be put away
prayers.text: Far be it from us to say that we will recompense evil, or that we should avenge ourselves. But we pray that all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil-speaking may be put away from us, with all malice; and that we may be kind one to another, and tender-hearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake we hope hath forgiven us. O make us merciful as our Father which is in heaven is merciful, who hath promised that with the merciful he will show himself merciful.
prayers.author: Matthew Henry

examinationQuestions: Whom are you holding something against today, and what wrong do you keep going back over in your mind?
What does your bitterness say about how you see God: that he did not see the wrong, or that he will not judge it rightly?
When you set the debt others owe you beside the debt Christ has forgiven you, how does it look?
Have you prayed for the one who hurt you, by name, and asked God to do that person good?
Has this bitterness spread? Have you spoken of the wrong to draw others to your side against the one who did it?

Is there a step toward peace you can take, as far as it depends on you? Forgiving does not mean calling the wrong small or putting yourself back in harm's way. If you have been abused, speak with your pastor.
fleeActions: Stop going over the wrong. Get up, leave the place where you are brooding, and do a task with your hands.
Pray out loud for the person who hurt you, by name, and ask God to bless them.
Do not send the message or make the call you are rehearsing. Put the phone away until you have prayed.
Read the parable in Matthew 18:21-35 slowly, and set your own debt to God beside the debt you are counting.
Call one of your brethren and ask for prayer to forgive. Ask for prayer, not for agreement against the one who wronged you.
Before you come to the Lord's Table this Lord's Day, seek peace with the one you are at odds with, if it is safe and wise to do so. Your pastor can help you.

afterFallReadings.text: The best way to separate things that are frozen, is by fire. When sin and the heart are frozen together, the best way to separate them is by the fire of love. Shall I sin against a gracious Father, and abuse that love which pardons me?
afterFallReadings.author: Thomas Watson

afterFallReadings.text: Manasseh was a crimson sinner; but when he humbled himself greatly, the golden sceptre of mercy was held forth. When his head was a fountain to weep for sin, Christ's side was a fountain to wash away sin. It is not the greatness of sin, but impenitence, that destroys.
afterFallReadings.author: Thomas Watson
